review_note: Management described challenging conditions, short-term demand contraction and reduced order books while explicitly prioritising cost control and margin protection; however, underlying margin improved 140bps to 7.4%, pre-tax cash generation increased and covenant net debt fell, providing strong but not fully dispositive contrary evidence.

The disclosure contained only routine operating pressure: Group gross and adjusted EBITDA margins were stable despite a three-point managed-services gross-margin decline, operating cash conversion was 84% with modest net debt, and 17% revenue growth plus 14% adjusted EBITDA growth supplied multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.

COVID-19 affected end markets, lengthened sales cycles and prompted prudent liquidity actions, but the precautionary facility draw was repaid in the second half; 115% cash conversion and a reduction in net debt from £49.4m to £9.9m supplied strong contrary evidence, while mixed segment margins kept the margin score at the lower stable-to-slightly-weaker anchor.

Difficult market conditions and a 19% MRP revenue decline led management to align that unit's cost base, with inflation and MRP weighing on adjusted EBITDA margin; Group gross margin nevertheless improved to 41%, operating cash conversion reached 96%, and strong KX and First Derivative growth supplied substantial contrary evidence.
